name: Joseph Chou
bio: Joseph Chou is the Republican nominee for New York's 6th Congressional District in 2026. Born in Japan, he immigrated to the United States as a child in 1974 and has run his own car repair business in Queens since 1990. His campaign says his Christian faith shapes his approach to public life.

platform.point: Seeks a balanced tax policy that eases burdens on working families and people starting small businesses.
Supports public, private and alternative schooling options, fair student loan interest rates, and vocational and arts programs in public schools.
Calls for secure borders combined with a compassionate approach to immigration, drawing on his own path to citizenship.
Wants to reform New York's cashless bail system while keeping room for rehabilitation.
Supports parental decision-making on education and health, better healthcare access and affordable childcare.
Honour the district's cultural diversity and promote unity among residents.
Base policy on Christian principles while seeking broad appeal.

economy.evidence: General statement: campaign seeks a balanced tax policy that lightens burdens on working families and small businesses.

welfare.evidence: General statement: campaign lists improved healthcare access and affordable childcare as goals.

security.evidence: General statement: campaign wants cashless bail reformed in a way balancing justice and rehabilitation, and closer local, state and federal cooperation against major crime.

immigration.evidence: General statement: campaign pairs secure borders with a compassionate approach to immigration.

education.evidence: General statement: campaign backs public, private and alternative schooling options and parental decision-making, while also supporting public school programs.

faith.evidence: Campaign says his policies will be guided by Christian principles.

notes: Read the campaign home, about and issues pages; web search was unavailable, so no news coverage or questionnaires were found. Abortion, guns, foreign policy, energy and tech positions remain unknown.

name: Melvin Rivera
bio: Melvin Rivera is a community activist and tenant organizer from Bushwick, Brooklyn, and the Republican nominee for New York's 7th congressional district. His campaign cites more than 30 years of community work, including tenant protection, Hurricane Maria relief and pandemic outreach with the city. His site describes him as running on accountability and free enterprise rather than party loyalty.

platform.point: Backs a Tenant Opportunity to Purchase Act giving tenants first right to buy their buildings, plus an anti-flip tax on speculation.
Wants benefits tied to apprenticeships, financial literacy and savings goals, letting families keep benefits while they start earning.
Focus enforcement on criminal offenders with warrants and create expedited green cards for long-term, tax-paying residents.
Fully fund law enforcement, raise officer pay and mental health support, and expand community policing.
Repeal New York's Taylor Law and protect workers' rights to organize, protest and negotiate wages.
Challenge monopolistic utilities such as National Grid, expand micro-loans, and cut unnecessary small business rules.
Supports reinstating the state stock transfer tax to pay for drinking water, stormwater and sewer upgrades.
Expand trade schools and apprenticeships, require financial literacy training, and give parents more say in schools.

economy.evidence: Campaign backs an anti-flip tax, reinstating a stock transfer tax and challenging utility monopolies, alongside trimming small business regulation.

welfare.evidence: Campaign wants public assistance tied to apprenticeships, financial literacy and savings targets to reduce dependency.

security.evidence: Campaign calls for fully funding law enforcement and raising officer pay while expanding community policing.

immigration.evidence: Campaign would limit enforcement to criminal offenders with warrants and create expedited green cards for residents of 10+ years.

energy.evidence: He organized opposition to the North Brooklyn Pipeline and his platform backs climate adaptation and air quality standards.

education.evidence: General statement: campaign favors trade schools and more parental and community control over schools, without mentioning vouchers.

notes: Read the campaign home, biography, issues and news pages; web search was unavailable and no questionnaire answers were found. Abortion, guns, foreign policy, tech and faith positions remain unknown.

name: Lewis Mizrahi
bio: Lewis Mizrahi is the Republican nominee for New York's 8th congressional district. He works as a criminal justice data analyst and wildland firefighter and attended John Jay College of Criminal Justice.
notes: Web search was unavailable; several likely campaign domains were checked and none belonged to him, and no questionnaire answers were found. Earlier coverage noted support for Second Amendment rights and local sheriffs, which alone is too narrow to score.

name: Joel Anabilah-Azumah
bio: Joel Anabilah-Azumah is the Republican nominee for New York's 9th congressional district. He owns a small business in Brooklyn, coaches men's volleyball at Brooklyn College, and holds a civil engineering degree from Union College. He has run for office several times before.

platform.point: Lower taxes, arguing people spend their money better than government.
Raise the federal minimum wage from $7.25 to $17 an hour so full-time workers can support families.
Support homeownership with less taxation and regulation.
Invest heavily in roads, rail, pipelines and nuclear power plants, including a Utica Avenue subway line.
Avoid major wars and foreign adventures so money can go to domestic infrastructure.
Warns that fast-learning AI systems could escape human oversight and government accountability.
Oppose censorship by government or technology companies.
Keep neighborhoods safe and community-invested.

economy.evidence: Campaign proposes raising the federal minimum wage from $7.25 to $17 an hour; the issues page states no tax position.

foreign.evidence: General statement: campaign says the US should avoid major conflicts and focus spending on domestic infrastructure.

energy.evidence: Campaign backs building pipelines and nuclear power plants as infrastructure investment.

tech.evidence: General statement: campaign warns AI could evade human oversight but names no specific regulation.

notes: Read the campaign home, biography, issues and news pages; web search was unavailable and the only news item was a 2022 radio interview. Immigration, abortion, guns, schools and faith positions remain unknown.

name: Mike Kirchner
bio: Mike Kirchner is a retired consulting actuary from Northeast Ohio who spent about 30 years valuing pension plans. He holds an applied mathematics degree from the University of Akron and won the 2026 Republican primary for Ohio's 11th congressional district. He has not held elected office.

platform.point: Says the country lacks a plan for Social Security's old-age and survivor program and has published a paper on it.
Favors more market competition to hold down prices.
Calls for direct, fact-based communication and less inflammatory rhetoric.
Supports immigration by people able to take part successfully in the economy.
Says he would concentrate on domestic issues rather than foreign policy, and takes no position on Middle East conflicts.
Lists personal responsibility as a secondary campaign theme.

notes: Read the campaign site, Vote411 answers and a Cleveland Jewish News candidate Q&A; his Social Security paper is a PDF that was not downloaded. His answers stay too general to score any topic.

name: Jen Mazzuckelli
bio: Jen Mazzuckelli is the Democratic nominee for Ohio's 2nd District and ran for Clermont County commissioner in 2024. She graduated from Illinois College, holds a master's degree in teaching from Miami University, and has worked as a high school English teacher and in human resources. She says she accepts only small-dollar donations.

platform.point: Wants the John Lewis Voting Rights Act and the For the People Act passed, and less big money in elections.
Prioritize reducing the deficit, have the wealthiest pay their fair share, and cut housing, healthcare and energy costs.
Revisit the 2024 bipartisan border bill, add immigration judges, fund CBP vetting, and keep the border open to lawful immigrants.
Base foreign policy on universal human rights and national sovereignty, using diplomacy before military force.
Treat substance abuse as a mental health issue rather than a criminal one.
Says she will represent working people over campaign donors and address families' economic hardship.
Points to gaps in how the justice system protects domestic violence victims.
Aims to reduce political division among residents of the district.

economy.evidence: In her Vote411 answers she says the wealthiest should pay their fair share of taxes, alongside cutting the deficit.

liberty.evidence: She objects to Christian nationalists making decisions for women (abortion) and wants substance abuse treated as a health issue (drugs).

immigration.evidence: She backs the 2024 bipartisan border bill, more immigration judges and CBP funding, but opposes closing the border.

faith.evidence: General statement: she says she ran partly because of Christian nationalist influence on government decisions.

notes: Used her campaign site, Vote411 answers, and WVXU and Marietta Times primary coverage. Her positions on welfare, energy, tech, schools and security remain unknown; her diplomacy-first foreign policy answer was too general to score.

name: Cleophus Dulaney
bio: Cleophus Dulaney is the Republican nominee for Ohio's 3rd District, which he also sought in 2020. He is a retired local business owner with more than 20 years of experience in operations management. His campaign describes long-running community work, including outreach to homeless residents and summer workshops for young people.

platform.point: Pause immigration and tighten vetting, admitting only people who are self-sufficient and not reliant on government support.
Wants voter ID, proof of citizenship, hand counts, no voting machines, and mail ballots only for limited cases.
Eliminate property taxes so government does not rely on homeowners' taxes, and stabilize the housing market.
Backs Medicare drug price negotiation, targeted tax relief for working families and no new loopholes for the wealthy.
Invest in infrastructure, advanced manufacturing and clean energy, expand apprenticeships, and cut red tape for small businesses.
Wants solutions to the affordable housing crisis and gentrification pressures in the district.
Seeks better relationships between the community and law enforcement.
Supports rehabilitation services addressing homelessness and opioid addiction.

economy.evidence: He mixes eliminating property taxes and cutting red tape with Medicare drug price negotiation and opposing tax loopholes for the wealthy.

immigration.evidence: In his Vote411 answers he calls for pausing current immigration policy, stricter vetting and admitting only self-sufficient newcomers.

energy.evidence: General statement: campaign lists clean energy among sectors for job investment.

notes: Used his campaign home and issues pages and his Vote411 answers; web search was unavailable. His abortion and gun survey answers could not be confirmed, so liberty stays unscored, and foreign policy, tech, schools and faith remain unknown.

name: Brian Shaver
bio: Brian Shaver is president of the Fostoria City Council, where he has served as an at-large member since 2013, and a social studies teacher at Fostoria Junior/Senior High School. He has led the Fostoria Education Association, the local teachers' union, since 2019. A lifelong Northwest Ohio resident, he won the 2026 Democratic primary for Ohio's 5th District.

platform.point: The wealthiest Americans should pay the same tax rate as everyone else, without loopholes that hide income.
Support farmers and the food supply, invest in affordable rural housing, and lower medication costs.
Congress should reassert its authority over offensive or preemptive military action and avoid using troops for domestic policing.
Wants a fair, humane immigration system that helps people contribute safely and legally.
Says voting rules belong to the states and that Ohio already verifies citizenship at registration.
Supports term limits for elected officials and limits on campaign finance.
Wants guardrails that stop elected officials from profiting from their positions and more legislative transparency.
Lists healthcare and prescription drug costs among his key campaign issues.

economy.evidence: In his Vote411 answers he says the wealthiest should pay the same rate as others with loopholes closed, and backs rural housing investment.

security.evidence: He objects to deploying troops for routine domestic policing and to blurring military and civilian roles.

immigration.evidence: General statement: he wants a fair, humane system that treats immigrants with dignity and helps them contribute legally.

foreign.evidence: He urges caution in using the military, a clear exit plan for any conflict, and congressional limits on preemptive action.

notes: Used his Vote411 answers and campaign site, whose issue pages (including guns, religion and education) are videos with no text. Positions on welfare, guns, abortion, energy, tech, schools and faith remain unknown.
